Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0754 PM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 250100Z - 251200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS
SOUTH-CENTRAL/EASTERN ND INTO NORTHERN MN AND EXTREME NORTHEAST
SD...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of large hail, damaging winds, and a
tornado risk remain possible this evening across portions of North
Dakota into northern Minnesota and extreme northeast South Dakota.

...ND into northern MN...
Scattered supercells are ongoing this evening across northern MN,
while a small storm cluster (with occasional embedded supercell
structures) is moving eastward across southeast ND and extreme
northeast SD. MLCAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of 40-50
kt will continue to provide a favorable environment for organized
storms through the evening, though some increase in CINH is expected
with time. Ongoing supercell structures will continue to pose a
threat of large hail and localized severe gusts, and some tornado
threat may persist through at least dusk, given increasing low-level
shear/SRH (as observed on the KMVX VWP). Any upscale growth could be
accompanied by localized swaths of greater severe-wind threat. An
eventual weakening trend is expected late tonight, as CINH continues
to increase with time and buoyancy decreases with southeastward
extent. See MCD 1726 and MCD 1727 for more information. 

...Elsewhere...
High-based convection may continue to pose a threat for localized
strong to severe gusts across parts of the southern Rockies and High
Plains, southeast AZ, and the northern Great Basin into parts of
ID/western WY/southwest MT though the evening. Weak deep-layer
flow/shear should continue to limit potential for a more organized
severe threat.

..Dean.. 07/25/2026

$$

Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1233 PM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ROM THE 
NORTHERN ROCKIES INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST...AND ACROSS PORTIONS OF
SOUTHEAST ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms will be possible from the northern Rockies
into the upper Midwest, and across portions of southeast Arizona.

...Synopsis...
A belt of enhanced mid-level flow will move around the northern
periphery of the high amplitude ridge across the central US
D2/Saturday. Southwesterly mid-level flow will overspread portions
of the northern Rockies, with more northwesterly flow shifting
across the Upper Midwest into the Great Lakes Region.  At the
surface, a weak front will extend from a surface low over the
northern and central Plains to the Southeast coastal areas. 

...Northern Rockies...
Deeply mixed boundary layer conditions are expected across the
Northern Rockies amid dry sub-cloud inverted-v soundings and steep
low to mid level lapse rates. Scattered afternoon thunderstorm
development is expected across the high terrain. Moderate
instability is progged along with strong deep layer shear, which may
support isolated stronger cells with potential for strong to severe
wind gusts.

...South Dakota and the Upper Midwest to the Great Lakes...
Strong daytime heating is expected across the northern Plains into
the Upper Midwest and Great Lakes Region. Daytime temperatures are
progged to possibly exceed 100 F south of the weak front from the
Dakotas into the Upper Midwest. With the building high amplitude
ridge, warming around the 850-700 mb level will result in capping
across much of the more strongly unstable air mass. It does appear
that portions of northern/central Minnesota into northern Wisconsin
and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan may see enough weakening of the
cap to allow for isolated thunderstorm development by the afternoon.
Forecast soundings suggest veering wind profiles favorable for
supercells. Strong deep layer shear and linearly elongated profiles
will support large to very large hail and damaging wind. Though
low-level shear is more marginal, low tornado potential will exist.

Additional isolated thunderstorms may develop near the Black Hills
in South Dakota. Very hot and moderately unstable conditions are
expected amid steep low to mid-level lapse rates. Isolated
supercells capable of large hail and damaging wind will be possible,
with potential for some clustering downstream and increase in
damaging wind potential into the evening. 

...Southeast Arizona...
The favorable position of the surface high across the Four Corners
will bring moist easterly flow across southeastern Arizona. Some
enhancement of the easterly flow will allow for modest shear
profiles. It is likely that storms will develop across the high
terrain and move into the low deserts through the afternoon/evening.
Deeply mixed profiles and modest shear for organization will support
potential for strong to severe winds.

..Thornton.. 07/24/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0228 PM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE UPPER
MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO UPPER MIDWEST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of mainly large hail and damaging winds
are possible from the upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into
portions of the mid Missouri Valley on Sunday and Sunday night.

...Synopsis...
Enhanced mid-level flow will round the central US ridge D3/Sunday,
overspreading portions of the Midwest and Great Lakes regions. Along
with the increasing flow, several shortwave disturbances will shift
across the region. At the surface, a low will develop across the
northern Plains/Upper Midwest with a surface front moving through
the northern Plains/Midwest by the evening.

...Upper Mississippi Valley into the Great Lakes...
Beneath strong upper-level ridging and a very moist air mass with
dew points in the 60s to mid 70s, an EML plume will advect eastward
across the High Plains into the Midwest/Great Lakes region. This
will result in a very volatile and strongly unstable but largely
capped air mass. While forcing for ascent will increase, lack of
discernible surface features and strength of the capping inversion
leads to low confidence in the exact evolution of thunderstorm
development. Hi-res guidance does suggest that a few isolated
supercells may develop. A conditional threat for large to very large
hail, damaging wind, and perhaps a tornado will exist with any
storms that can become rooted within the boundary layer, given the
presence of 35-50 kt deep-layer shear and the favorable unstable air
mass. 

As the front shifts south and east through the afternoon/evening and
forcing for ascent increases, storms may develop as far west as the
eastern Dakotas/Nebraska. It seems probable that a thunderstorm
complex could develop across some portion of the upper Mississippi
Valley, though confidence in the exact corridor remains low. This
will pose a conditional threat for a more focused corridor of
damaging wind potential.

..Thornton.. 07/24/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0337 AM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 271200Z - 011200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Monday...
A prominent upper high will remain centered over the central and
southern Plains with a belt of enhanced mid-level flow forecast
along the periphery of that feature from the northern Plains into
the Great Lakes. Within that flow regime, a short-wave trough is
forecast to translate through the Great Lakes in tandem with a
surface low and trailing cold front. A hot and moist boundary layer
is expected ahead of the front, yielding moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Despite veered low-level winds,
strengthening mid/upper-level winds in the exit region of a jet
streak will contribute to sufficient vertical shear for organized
severe storms across portions of the Great Lakes into the OH Valley
Monday afternoon into night.


...Day 5/Tuesday...
The Day 4/Monday short-wave trough is forecast to evolve into an
upper low across southwest ON and the lower Great Lakes with an
associated belt of stronger cyclonic flow developing from the OH
Valley into the southern Mid-Atlantic and NC. At the surface, an
area of low pressure will develop from the lower Great Lakes into
central NY with a trailing cold front advancing through the upper OH
Valley, central Appalachians, and Mid-Atlantic.

Thunderstorms may be ongoing Tuesday morning along and ahead of the
front from the lower Great Lakes and upper OH Valley into the
Mid-Atlantic. Stronger heating is anticipated to the south of the
early-day storms from the southern Mid-Atlantic into NC, where
moderate to potentially strong instability is forecast. The
strongest instability will coincide with modestly strong deep-layer
shear to support some severe weather threat in those areas Tuesday
afternoon and evening.


...Days 6-8/Wednesday-Friday...
The 00Z ensemble means depict a slight westward regression of the
dominant mid/upper-level high with persistent troughing along the
East Coast. On the periphery of the high, a notable short-wave
trough is forecast to progress from the Canadian Rockies on
Wednesday through the Prairie Provinces on Thursday with modest
height falls along the international border. By Friday, there is
some model signal for another short-wave trough to move into the
upper MS Valley and Great Lakes regions. At the surface, a more
substantial cold front is projected to move into the northern Plains
on Thursday, and the upper Midwest and Great Lakes by Friday. 

A few severe storms appear possible in the Southeast and northern
Plains on Wednesday, the northern Plains on Thursday, and the upper
Midwest into the Great Lakes on Friday. Confidence in the magnitude
and areal extent of the threat is currently too low to delineate
additional areas.

..Mead.. 07/24/2026
